reference_title: Eurocode 7: Geotechnical design - Part 2: Ground investigation and testing

sections.title: General requirements
sections.summary: Investigation results go in the Ground Investigation Report, part of the Geotechnical Design Report: a presentation of the geotechnical information and an evaluation stating the assumptions; it may include derived values, states known limitations and should propose further investigations with a programme.
sections.body: (1)P Results of a geotechnical investigation shall be compiled in the Ground Investigation Report, which forms part of the Geotechnical Design Report. (2)P It shall consist of a presentation of all appropriate geotechnical information, including geological features and relevant data, and a geotechnical evaluation of it, stating the assumptions made in interpreting the tests. (3) It may be one report or separate parts. (4) It may include derived values. (5)P It shall state known limitations of the results where appropriate. (6) It should propose needed further field and laboratory investigations, justifying them, with a detailed programme. (p. 95)
key_points: Ground Investigation Report is part of the Geotechnical Design Report (p. 95).
Presentation of information plus evaluation stating assumptions (p. 95).
State known limitations; propose further investigation with a programme (p. 95).
sections.applicability: Defines the mandatory content and role of the Ground Investigation Report within the overall Geotechnical Design Report.

sections.title: Presentation of geotechnical information
sections.summary: The presentation is a factual account of all field and laboratory work: purpose and scope, geotechnical category, consultants and subcontractors, dates, and site reconnaissance (groundwater, neighbouring structures, exposures, instability, mining, excavation, history, geology, survey, air photos, local experience, seismicity), with methods, procedures and results reported per the EN and ISO standards used.
sections.body: (1)P The presentation shall include a factual account of all field and laboratory investigations. (2) It should give, as relevant: purpose and scope, with the site and topography, the planned structure and the planning stage; the geotechnical category; names of consultants and subcontractors; dates of field and laboratory work; field reconnaissance of the site and surroundings noting a) evidence of groundwater, b) behaviour of neighbouring structures, c) exposures in quarries and borrow areas, d) areas of instability, e) exposures of mining activity, f) excavation difficulties, g) site history, h) geology including faulting, i) survey data with plans of the structure and all investigation points, j) aerial photograph information, k) local experience, l) seismicity (p. 95). (3)P It shall document methods, procedures and results, including reports of desk studies, field investigations (sampling, field tests, groundwater measurements) and laboratory tests. (4)P Field and laboratory results shall be presented and reported per the EN and/or ISO standards applied (p. 96). (pp. 95 to 96)
key_points: Factual account of all field and laboratory work (p. 95).
Site reconnaissance items a) to l), groundwater to seismicity (p. 95).
Report results per the EN and ISO standards applied (p. 96).
sections.applicability: Specifies the factual (as opposed to interpretive) content required in the Ground Investigation Report.

sections.title: Evaluation of geotechnical information
sections.summary: The evaluation is documented: results per Sections 3 to 5, review of 6.2, strata geometry, properties, irregularities, allowance for groundwater, drilling, sampling and handling, cross-sections, parameter values per stratum and review of derived values; averaging can hide weak zones; similar strata or fine layer sequences may be one stratum; boundaries may be interpolated linearly if justified.
sections.body: (1)P The documented evaluation shall include as appropriate: field and laboratory results evaluated per Sections 3 to 5; review of the results and all other information in 6.2; strata geometry; detailed descriptions of all strata with physical, deformation and strength properties; comments on irregularities such as cavities and discontinuous zones. (2)P Where appropriate, it shall be documented that interpretation allowed for groundwater table, ground type, drilling and sampling methods, transport, handling and preparation, and that the strata assumed from desk studies and inspections were reconsidered against the results. (3) Documentation should include as appropriate: tables and graphs of results in cross-sections showing strata, boundaries and groundwater table relative to the project; parameter values per stratum; review of derived values (see 6.4). (4) Averaging can mask a weaker zone and should be used with caution; weak zones must be identified; parameter variations can signal significant changes in site conditions. (5) Results should be compared with experience for each parameter, with special attention to anomalous results against other tests measuring the same parameter. (6) It should substantiate that strata whose parameters differ only slightly may be taken as one (p. 96). (7) A sequence of fine layers of very different composition or properties may be one stratum if the overall behaviour governs and parameters chosen for it represent that behaviour. (8) Layer boundaries and groundwater level may be interpolated linearly between investigation points if spacing is small enough and geology homogeneous enough; such interpolation and its justification should be reported (p. 97). (pp. 96 to 97)
key_points: Averaging can mask weak zones; identify them (p. 96).
Slightly differing strata may be one stratum (p. 96).
Linear interpolation between points if close and homogeneous, reported (p. 97).
sections.applicability: Specifies the interpretive content and cautions (averaging, stratum lumping, interpolation) required in the Ground Investigation Report's evaluation section.

sections.title: Establishment of derived values
sections.summary: Where correlations derive geotechnical parameters or coefficients, the correlations and their applicability are documented.
sections.body: (1)P If correlations were used to derive geotechnical parameters or coefficients, the correlations and their applicability shall be documented. (p. 97)
key_points: Document correlations used and their applicability (p. 97).
sections.applicability: Closes the loop from Section 1.6's derived-value framework back into mandatory reporting, ensuring traceability of every correlation used in design.
